To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• Computational thinking (CT) is not the same as computer science (CS).

(i) the two most common approaches to teaching CS are the "traditional" one and the "new" one; (ii) the traditional approach is based on a narrow view of CS and is not suitable for teaching CS in schools; and (iii) the new approach, which is based on Wing's CT, is a diluted version of CS, which is not a suitable approach for teaching CS either.
• The two main approaches for teaching CT are the CT as thinking patterns approach, which is based on the Wing model, and the CT as a process approach, which is rooted in Papert's model.

how to teach CS to students in grades 5–12, and how to prepare teachers to teach CS to these grades.
